question: How many fundamental duties were added in the Indian Constitution in 1976?
solution:
The correct answer is __**option 4**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The 42nd Amendment Act of 1976 added ten fundamental duties to the Indian Constitution.
 
• These duties are enshrined in Part IV-A of the Constitution under Article 51A.
 
• The fundamental duties were added based on the recommendations of the Swaran Singh Committee.
 
• These duties emphasize the moral obligations of all citizens to help promote a spirit of patriotism and uphold the unity of India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **42nd Amendment Act:**

 
 
• This amendment is known as the "Mini-Constitution" due to its extensive changes to the Constitution.
 
• It was enacted during the Emergency period (1975-1977) under Prime Minister Indira Gandhi.
 
• It attempted to reduce the power of the judiciary and increase the power of the Parliament.
 
 
 
• **Article 51A:**
 
 
• Article 51A specifies the fundamental duties of every citizen of India.
 
• These duties include respect for the Constitution, the national flag, and the national anthem.
 
 
 
• **Swaran Singh Committee:**
 
 
• This committee was formed in 1976 to make recommendations about fundamental duties and other constitutional amendments.
 
• It was headed by Sardar Swaran Singh, a prominent Congress leader.
 
 
 
• **Importance of Fundamental Duties:**
 
 
• They serve as a constant reminder to citizens to be responsible and active participants in the democratic process.
 
• Fundamental duties are non-justiciable, meaning they are not enforceable by the courts.
